races.name: Ebf Restricted Maiden Fillies' Stakes (for Horses In Bands B, C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Ric And Mary Hambro Aphrodite Fillies' Stakes (Listed Race) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Brielle
runners_data.note: Showed a strong win over 10f on good ground and carries a hood, but her natural front-tracking style has been displaced by a fuller complement of prominent types; rated a style fit of 0.92, she may find herself wider and less comfortable than ideal over a trip that stretches her.|
runners_data.comment: Sixth last time was below her level, though that followed a win two starts back and two victories in her last five starts. She has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 96 leaves her mid-pack in this field.

runners_data.name: Club Class
runners_data.note: Consistent performer with five top-four finishes in recent starts, all on Flat/Standard; her true stalking style is similarly squeezed in this field, and the step up to Listed company looks demanding for an OR-81 filly racing outside her comfort zone positionally.|
runners_data.comment: Frustratingly consistent without a win, with three seconds and two fourths in her last five starts, second again last time out. She has run over today's trip and going before, but ranked seventh of nine on a rating of 91, she looks held on these figures.

runners_data.name: Little Dorrit
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's hold-up filly has decent form at this trip, including a Listed win over 11f on standard ground, but four blank runs on good ground since that win is a meaningful concern and she needs a stronger gallop than Tribal Queen is likely to set to get competitive.|
runners_data.comment: Little Dorrit's yard is in excellent form, striking at 26 percent in the last fortnight, and she rates second-best of these at 101. She has run over today's trip and going before, but her level has dipped since a win five starts back, with fifth last time out following an eighth two starts back.

runners_data.name: Naga
runners_data.note: Has two wins on good ground at shorter trips and showed progressive form earlier this season; naturally a front-tracker, she is likely to be pushed into an unfamiliar midfield position by Tribal Queen's presence, carrying a style-fit discount of 0.93 that tempers confidence in her producing her best.|
runners_data.comment: Naga strung together three straight wins before her recent dip, finishing third and fourth in her last two starts. She has run over today's trip and going before and carries a rating of 98, but a 49-day absence since her last run is a query fitness-wise.

runners_data.name: Orionis
runners_data.note: William Haggas filly with three wins on good/good-to-firm at 12f — the best profile in the race for this exact surface and trip; tracked the pace effectively in all her wins and is perfectly suited to sitting just off Tribal Queen before quickening.|
runners_data.comment: Orionis was a winner two starts back and again four starts back, with only a below-par seventh last time out disrupting an otherwise progressive profile. She has run over today's trip and going before, rated 99 - third-best in this field - with more expected on a return to form.

runners_data.name: Revoir
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's consistent placed performer on good ground, but she has yet to win at this level or above and her finishing positions are dominated by near misses rather than decisive victories; pattern-hood worn, suggesting connections are working on concentration.|
runners_data.comment: Revoir has been the model of consistency without quite getting up, three seconds and a third from her last five starts, second again last time out. She has run over today's trip and going before, and with her trainer among the form yards at 31 percent, rates the best of these nine at 110.

runners_data.name: Fashion's Fancy
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's lightly raced three-year-old carries weight relief and has already won over 10f on soft before a placed effort on standard; 57 days off is the only question but Appleby routinely produces horses fresh, and her profile fits a pace-dependent steadily-run race.|
runners_data.comment: Fashion's Fancy is lightly raced, but her recent form reads well: a third followed by a win last time out. A rating of just 70, though, leaves her second-bottom in this field, and a 57-day absence adds another question mark despite her trainer's form figures (26% last fortnight).

runners_data.name: K Sarra
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old won over 8f on standard ground but has been beaten at long odds in a 12f handicap on soft most recently; the step into Listed company over a trip that remains unproven looks like a reach at this stage of her development.|
runners_data.comment: K Sarra won four starts back, since finishing unplaced, third, and eighth last time out - a form dip that leaves this rating of 98 hard to fully trust. Her trainer is among the in-form yards at 31 percent in the last fortnight, some compensation after a 43-day absence.

runners_data.name: Tribal Queen
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's confirmed front-runner who won over 11f on standard — she takes on the role of sole pace-maker and on good-to-firm ground over a flat track she can control the race completely; the key risk is whether she can extend her winning run into Listed territory at the longer trip.|
runners_data.comment: Tribal Queen was a winner last time out having been third the run before, but she rates bottom of the weights in this field at 69 on our figures. Her trainer is among the in-form yards at 26 percent in the last fortnight, offering some encouragement, and a 38-day break should have her fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Tribal Queen is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival prepared to press her from the front, she is set to control this race at a sustainable gallop over Newmarket's July Course mile-and-a-half. Good to Firm ground and a flat, uncontested lead suits a horse that can dictate tempo, meaning the fractions are unlikely to be truly severe — Tribal Queen can bowl along well within herself and still hold a meaningful advantage turning for home. The field contains a glut of prominent-leaning types — Naga, Brielle, and Club Class are all natural stalkers who are realistically going to find themselves shuffled into a midfield role they don't naturally inhabit, making the race shape more compressed behind the leader than the raw pace figures suggest. This race shape most clearly favours a prominent or lead-tracking horse that can sit just off Tribal Queen, control its own energy expenditure, and produce a clean sustained finish — in other words, Orionis and Fashion's Fancy, both of whom are built for exactly this kind of measured, front-dominated contest on fast ground.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tribal Queen Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Tribal Queen leads without meaningful pressure and the pace is controlled throughout, setting a falsely steady tempo.
scenarios.body: Tribal Queen rolls along in front at a comfortable clip, the field stacks up behind her in a compact unit, and the race becomes a sprint for home from the two-furlong pole; horses with a clean passage close to the pace who can quicken on fast ground are best placed. Fashion's Fancy and Orionis, sitting just behind the lead with clean running, are ideally suited to pounce as the tempo quickens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Burst
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely modest and the race degenerates into a late dash from the two-furlong marker.
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo compresses the field further, removing any advantage for hold-up horses and turning this into a flat-out sprint finish where speed rather than stamina decides it; Orionis and Revoir, both consistent finishers at this trip on good ground, are well placed to deliver a sharp late effort. K Sarra is unlikely to benefit from a sprint finish given her inconsistent recent form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or a genuine gap opens late for a horse ridden with patience from the rear.
scenarios.body: Little Dorrit or K Sarra would need a strong enough gallop to create the separation required for a big finishing run, but with Tribal Queen likely to set only a fair tempo this scenario is structurally disadvantaged in this field. The redistributed midfield runners are not true hold-up types, making it harder for genuine closers to exploit a gap that may never fully materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the glut of natural front-runners — Naga, Brielle, Club Class — all push forward and force a pace battle for position in the early stages.
scenarios.body: An unexpected flare-up in pace as multiple prominent types refuse their mapped midfield role could string the field out and benefit a horse like Naga, who is effective on good ground and has the class to manage a stronger gallop. However, this scenario is heavily discounted because these horses are likely to accept midfield positions under race conditions given the presence of a dominant lead horse.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Naga, Brielle, or Club Class push forward from their mapped midfield positions at the start — if two or more refuse to settle, an unexpected pace flare could materially alter the race shape.|
Fashion's Fancy has had 57 days off since her last run; watch her in the pre-parade ring for any signs of freshness or agitation that could affect how Connor Planas rides her in the first furlong.|

Little Dorrit has gone 0-from-4 on ground good or better — if the going is confirmed good-to-firm as the report suggests, her hold-up style combined with a suspect going profile makes her difficult to support.|

Tribal Queen's sectionals from her 11f win should be studied — if she tends to set a flat, even-tempo gallop rather than a true pace, the field could compress two furlongs out and make this a luck-in-running contest for those trapped in traffic.|

Orionis is 0-from-7 when finishing seventh or worse, but 3-from-4 on good/good-to-firm at 12f — the going confirmation matters enormously for assessing whether her course-and-distance profile is truly live here.|

races.name: Lettergold Plastics Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Flag Of St George
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing 5-year-old whose two placing efforts at Sandown on similar ground give Jane Chapple-Hyam's runner strong course-and-distance profile credentials; 169 days off the track is the main query but the light weight and Paddy Bradley booking suggest he's ready to go.
runners_data.comment: Flag Of St George was only eighth last time out after a lengthy 169-day absence, though he was runner-up three and five starts back, and he has raced over today's trip and ground before. A strong speed figure is a point in his favour, but sitting down our order and off such a long layoff, he's hard to trust from stall seven.

runners_data.name: I Still Have Faith
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams's 6-year-old has run well at the top of the market before on Good and Good to Firm ground (2nd at Sandown on similar going), travels prominently and benefits directly from this pace shape; the tongue-tie is a positive headgear flag and Ray Dawson has won twice from three rides for this stable recently.
runners_data.comment: I Still Have Faith boasts a strong speed figure and experience over today's trip and ground. A second five starts back shows the level he can hit, though a moderate sixth last time out is the concern, and he returns 23 days later from stall two among the leading contenders here.

runners_data.name: Warrior Mode
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's hold-up operator has been off 255 days — a significant concern — but his profile shows a win on 7f at Sandown Stalls and he does go well fresh for this yard; Luke Morris will need the pace to have truly told by the final furlong for his late run to count.
runners_data.comment: Warrior Mode won five starts back, following up with a fourth and then a third, useful recent-form claims on our book. He has run over today's trip before and carries 135 lb from stall three, but a 255-day absence and a well-below-par effort last time out are the main concerns.

runners_data.name: Bell Shot
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 7-year-old is at heart a come-from-behind type who has won twice from hold-up positions, but with several natural hold-up horses in this field he will be operating closer to midfield than ideal, diluting the punchline of his style; Robert Havlin's ring-craft may help him find a better position than the race shape would naturally offer.
runners_data.comment: Bell Shot was third last time out and again three starts back, showing he retains ability despite finishes as low as ninth in this sequence. He has raced over today's trip and ground before, fresh 17 days on, though the yard is out of form at 1 from 26 in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Where's Freddy
runners_data.note: Another Stuart Williams hold-up runner who will find himself shuffled into midfield rather than settling at the rear as he prefers, given the depth of the hold-up contingent; fitted with both tongue-tie and headgear, his form over 7f is less convincing than over 8f, adding a trip concern alongside the positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Where's Freddy was only fourth last time out after two unplaced efforts before that, though a third four starts back is the standout form in this sequence. He has raced over today's trip and ground before, but sits bottom of these ratings from stall five with plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Jumby
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's 8-year-old has failed to win in 10 runs on Good ground, posting a string of mid-pack finishes at this track; Oliver Carmichael's 7lb claim helps the handicapper's view, but Jumby's hold-up style is a structural disadvantage in this pace shape and the form string gives little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Jumby boasts the fastest speed figure in this field, and the yard is red-hot at 8 from 31 (26%) in the last fortnight. He has raced over today's trip and ground before and carries top weight of 140 lb accordingly, with modest recent finishes the only knock after 70 days off - the clear one to beat on this evidence.

runners_data.name: Miletus
runners_data.note: James Keane's 5-year-old is the confirmed front-runner and wears a tongue-tie, having won over 7f on Good ground and shown he can make all effectively; the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence in him winning because front-runners who don't maintain dominance tend to be swept aside, but his role as pace-setter makes him central to every scenario.
runners_data.comment: Miletus won last time out, adding to two runner-up efforts across his last six starts. He has raced over today's trip and ground before and returns 29 days later from stall one, with only a below-par sixth three starts back to niggle.

races.paceDynamic: Miletus is the confirmed lone front-runner here, likely to stride into an uncontested lead from the outset on Good to Firm ground over Newmarket's straight seven furlongs, setting a sustainable gallop without any genuine pace rival to harry or quicken past him. Flag Of St George and I Still Have Faith are the main prominent types who will look to track him closely through the early stages, shaping this into an orderly procession rather than a scramble for the front. The hold-up contingent — Warrior Mode, Jumby — will have genuine ground to make up in the closing stages, while Bell Shot and Where's Freddy, despite being natural hold-up horses, are mapped into midfield because the field contains more rear-division types than can realistically settle at the back, meaning their true closing kick may be partially compromised. This race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently — the uncontested, measured pace set by Miletus rewards those sitting just behind him in the slipstream, with Flag Of St George and I Still Have Faith ideally placed to pounce; pure hold-up horses face an uphill task on a track that has been riding fast and offers little late cover.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Miletus Leads, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Miletus controls the tempo unchallenged and the race develops into a true test of cruising speed in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Miletus sets an honest but unforced pace and the horses camped just behind him — Flag Of St George and I Still Have Faith — get a perfect tow into contention, enabling them to produce their finishing efforts from an ideal position without burning energy early. On Good to Firm Newmarket ground, where the pace rarely truly collapses, horses who travel prominently into the final two furlongs consistently hold an advantage over those making ground from behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Miletus Wins Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Miletus's gallop is just quick enough to burn off the prominent holders without being so fast that it invites a late challenge.
scenarios.body: Miletus, having made all and controlled every fractions, simply finds enough in the tank around the two-furlong marker to repel I Still Have Faith and Flag Of St George, whose effort arrives fractionally too late. James Keane's runner has a strong record of winning over 7f on Good ground and the lack of any pressure through the race means this scenario is a genuine threat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If Miletus's early fractions are deceptively quick and the field strings out, leaving something in the tank for the hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Warrior Mode — who won on 7f at Sandown — and Jumby need the pace to have been stronger than it looks for their late runs to count, but on fast ground at Newmarket neither has shown the form to bridge a significant gap. Bell Shot, technically a hold-up type though mapped to midfield, might find himself best placed of the rear group if the front two tire.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is so slow that the race degenerates into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole, scrambling all positional plans.
scenarios.body: In a true sprint-home scenario the highest-rated horse Jumby or a fresh Bell Shot could theoretically grab a share, but neither has the turn-of-foot form on quick Newmarket ground to make this truly convincing. This is the least-likely shape given Miletus's front-running mandate and the presence of two prominent types pressing him.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether I Still Have Faith or Flag Of St George is able to press Miletus immediately after the break — if both lock on to him simultaneously, the race becomes a tactical tussle rather than a controlled solo lead.

Warrior Mode's 255-day absence is the longest gap in the field; Sir Mark Prescott horses often return well fresh, but if he shows any ring-rustiness in the opening furlong his hold-up style leaves no margin for error.

Bell Shot and Where's Freddy are genuine hold-up horses racing out of their preferred position — if they settle in midfield rather than at the rear they may peak too soon, flattening out in the final furlong rather than delivering their customary late burst.

Monitor the draw and early positioning from Miletus's stall — if he is slow out of the gate and any of the prominent types jumps him, the entire pace dynamic reverses and the scenario probabilities shift materially toward a contested-pace shape.

races.name: Club 26 At Ascot Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Westmorian
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who needs to dictate from the front; Grant Tuer stable in decent form (4/11 T14) but recent form figures of 0R-874 are discouraging and sim-going returns show just 0W0P in 15 comparable efforts — only live if given a completely uncontested lead.
runners_data.comment: Westmorian showed clear improvement last time out, a fourth having followed a run of below-par efforts including a refusal four starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before, and though yet to win in this sequence, the upward trend on a 17-day turnaround makes him the highest-rated of these eight at 84 and the one to beat on figures.

runners_data.name: Yes I'm Mali
runners_data.note: David Tudhope rides a horse with consistent 6f Good-ground form and three placed efforts in last five sim-going runs; genuine hold-up operator who will appreciate anything that sets a meaningful tempo, and the sim-going record of 1W3P is solid.
runners_data.comment: Yes I'm Mali won six starts back and has been running well again of late, second last time out having also been runner-up four starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before, rated 80 with a speed figure of 87, third-best in this field on our numbers.

runners_data.name: Expert Agent
runners_data.note: Won twice from six starts on Good going at this distance (1W2P in sim-going) and finished first or second at 6f on Good four times in last five qualifying runs — a true closer who needs a proper gallop but has the course-and-distance credentials to threaten.
runners_data.comment: Expert Agent was a winner two starts back and again four starts back, sandwiching a second in between, before a below-par sixth last time out. He has run over today's trip and going before and is second-best of these on a rating of 81, with the form to bounce back if repeating his best.

runners_data.name: Fenlander
runners_data.note: Christian Howarth (3) takes the mount for Pam Sly (0/2 T14, small yard) but Fenlander's form is exceptional — three consecutive wins, all at 6f on Good, with an 11/15 sim-going score of 3W7P; the most in-form runner in the field and ideally positioned to race just off the slow pace.
runners_data.comment: Fenlander arrives on a hat-trick, winning his last three starts in a row after finishing sixth, third and second before that. Impressive as that sequence reads, our figures rate him only 68 here, second-bottom of this field, suggesting those wins came in weaker company than he meets today.

runners_data.name: Dashing Dick
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old equipped with a hood; naturally a deep hold-up type but the excess of closers in this field means he is squeezed forward of his preferred position, and his recent form (8-8-7-3-6) on Good ground is limited — STYLE_FIT discount applies and 0W3P in sim-going offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Dashing Dick is winless in his last five starts, with a best of third two starts back the standout amid four finishes of sixth or worse, including sixth last time out. He has run over today's trip and going before, but a modest rating of 73 - sixth-best of these eight - makes him hard to fancy on figures alone.

runners_data.name: Lili Marleen
runners_data.note: Returned from a 79-day absence with a fall last time (F in form) and steps sharply back from 8f-11f to 6f, a trip she has only contested once on Synthetic; a genuine hold-up mare by nature but will be unable to get to the rear she needs here, and sim-going figures of 0W0P from just one comparable run add significant uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Lili Marleen has shown promise in patches, a win three starts back preceded by two thirds, but she was unplaced next time and fell when last seen. She has been off for 79 days, and with too little to judge her fully, she remains open to improvement on this unexposed profile.

runners_data.name: Spring Bloom
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a remarkable placed record — 0W5P in 11 sim-going runs — who will be denied her natural trailing position by the hold-up cluster but has the consistency to make use of a midfield slot; 29 days since last run is fine and John Butler (6/14 T14) is in fair form.
runners_data.comment: Spring Bloom keeps knocking on the door without getting his head in front, three seconds from his last five starts including when runner-up last time out. He has run over today's trip and going before, and a strong speed figure of 83 hints at more than his rating of 74 suggests, though he remains without a win in this sequence.

runners_data.name: Generous Rascal
runners_data.note: Three-year-old wearing a hood who has placed three times in five runs but not yet won; Dylan Cunha yard is cold (0/13 T14) and sim-going score of 0W0P from three applicable runs is modest — will race prominently and can pick up minor spoils if the winner falters but lacks the win-form to inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Generous Rascal has been fairly consistent without a win, three thirds among his last five starts, though an eighth and a below-par fifth - last time out - are the blemishes. He has run over today's trip and going before and rates 77 here, fourth-best of these on our figures, a leading threat if bouncing back to his best.

races.paceDynamic: Westmorian is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 6f Newmarket handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the gates rather than a scorching pace. Fenlander is the key prominent challenger and should sit close to Westmorian's quarters, with Generous Rascal also likely to race in the first half of the field, meaning the shape from flag to finish is a compressed, measured tempo with a small pace group and the bulk of the field sitting mid-to-rear. The race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or with cover in a controlled race and deliver sustained finishing kicks — deep hold-up types who need a true end-to-end gallop to close ground will find this pace insufficient. The field contains more hold-up types than the rear positions can accommodate: Dashing Dick, Lili Marleen, and Spring Bloom are all genuine closers who will be squeezed into midfield positions, with Spring Bloom — the most consistent placed horse of the trio and proven on this going — best placed to secure a useful pitch, but none of the three will be able to fully express their natural style.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Westmorian dictates a steady-to-honest tempo unchallenged and the race compresses into a sprint finish from 2f out.
scenarios.body: Fenlander, in career-best form with three consecutive wins and excellent course-and-distance figures on this going, travels close to the pace and has the most to draw on turning in; Generous Rascal, also racing prominently, could pick up the pieces if the winner weakens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Close Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to string out the field and create a genuine closing opportunity for the rear trio.
scenarios.body: Expert Agent has strong 6f form on Good ground with recent wins at this course and distance and is the most reliable closer in the field; Yes I'm Mali has solid sim-going figures and Daniel Tudhope aboard to maximise any late run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Two Tire
scenarios.trigger: If Fenlander pushes up to press Westmorian harder than expected and both leaders hit the rising ground cooked.
scenarios.body: Spring Bloom has relentless placed form at this level and on Good ground and, sitting a length or two closer than Dashing Dick and Lili Marleen, is first to benefit from a capitulation at the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Westmorian Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so gentle that Westmorian steals a break and converts front-running dominance without being seriously challenged.
scenarios.body: Westmorian's STYLE_FIT flag is a genuine caution and recent form is modest, but a truly uncontested lead on Good-to-Firm conditions gives any pace-setter a chance to last home.

watchPoints.text: Fenlander is the standout in-form runner — three straight wins at 6f Good and a clean sim-going profile — and if Christian Howarth (3) slots him neatly behind the gentle pace of Westmorian, he is the most dangerous horse in the field.
Lili Marleen's fitness is unproven after 79 days off, a fall last time out, and a sharp drop to 6f from much longer trips — watch market moves closely as she may need this run to find her feet.

Dashing Dick and Spring Bloom are both natural hold-up horses forced into midfield positions; if neither can find their rhythm and the pace fails to collapse, neither may generate the finish they need — watch how they jump and settle in the first furlong.

Going is confirmed Good to Firm for this race despite the headline "Good" description — that quicker surface suits horses with recent Good-to-Firm experience and may stretch the stamina of the older hold-up types on the short 6f Newmarket straight.

races.name: National Stud "Confined" Handicap Stakes (For Horses With No More Than One Win)

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Avenger
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on good ground last time out and has placed form at the same track and trip combination; Hector Crouch is an excellent tactician for falsely-run races and Michael Bell's yard is in modest nick (1/16 over 14 days), but the horse's natural hold-up style suits a sprint finish better than most rivals here and the sim-going record (3 from 6) is the strongest in the field.
runners_data.comment: Ziggy's Avenger won two starts back after a third three starts back, form that outweighs a below-par fifth last time out. He has raced over today's going before, returns from stall one carrying 135 lb, with a below-par eighth four starts back the only blot.

runners_data.name: Flag Of Eva
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 3yo has modest recent form (6-6-3) but the placed effort at 10f on good ground shows she stays this trip; Edward Greatrex takes over and has the experience to position her forward in a field of reluctant leaders, which is her best chance given her natural rear-of-field inclination.
runners_data.comment: Flag Of Eva was third last time out but twice sixth in the two starts before that, and the yard is out of form at 1 from 26 (4%) in the last fortnight. Though he has run over today's trip, a modest speed figure leaves him bottom of these ratings from stall three.

runners_data.name: Madjid
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton has been active recently (2/14 over 14 days) and Cieren Fallon is a significant booking, but this horse's true preference is to race from the back — being shuffled into a midfield position purely by default rather than design is a genuine concern, and his sim-going record (5 from 7 runs on similar going) does at least confirm he handles the conditions.
runners_data.comment: Madjid boasts the standout speed figure in this field and has raced over today's distance and going before, fresh again 16 days after his latest run. Recent form is patchy - seventh last time out, ninth three starts back - but a second four starts back underlines the level, and he tops our figures here.

runners_data.name: John Harrison
runners_data.note: David Probert partners this Alan King 3yo who showed a placed effort at 8f on good ground and has snippets of form suggesting he can quicken, but he is inherently a deep-seated hold-up horse forced toward a position that does not reflect how he wants to race; King's 14-day figures are blank (0/12) which adds a layer of caution.
runners_data.comment: John Harrison has been fairly consistent - third last time out, fourth before that, and a second three starts back - and he has raced over today's going before, fresh again 18 days on. A below-par eighth four starts back is the one blot, from 129 lb at stall four.

runners_data.name: Pipily
runners_data.note: Steps up from sprint distances (6-7f) to 10f for the first time and that trip extension is unproven; the headgear flag (p) suggests connections are searching for improvement, and while Ray Dawson is a capable claimer, Pipily's single run on similar going (1 from 4) and the style redistribution mean she faces a demanding ask on multiple fronts.
runners_data.comment: Pipily has yet to find the frame in her last four starts, seventh last time out having been fourth and sixth in the two before that. A modest speed figure leaves her down our order from 128 lb at stall two, returning 32 days on.

runners_data.name: Moon Warp
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's operation is rarely represented by horses returning from 318-day absences without a strong chance, and the trainer's 14-day strike rate (3/12) merits respect; however, Moon Warp fades in the finish, has shown concerning tendency to weaken late in previous runs, and the long break combined with a natural hold-up style in a race lacking genuine pace makes a winning return very hard to construct.
runners_data.comment: Moon Warp has raced over today's going before and posted a fair fourth four starts back, form that stands out among modest recent runs. He was unplaced last time out and hasn't run for 318 days, leaving fitness the obvious question, though he does hold the fourth-best figure here at 127 lb from stall five.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and every declared runner carrying a hold-up profile, this race faces a fundamental tactical vacuum — nobody wants to make the running, and the early stages at Newmarket's July course over 1m2f are likely to be crawled through as riders wait on each other. The result will almost certainly be a dawdle into the straight followed by a compressed, sprint-like finish off a slow tempo, with stamina becoming largely irrelevant and a sharp turn of foot from a handy position proving decisive. Ziggy's Avenger and Flag Of Eva, the two runners whose hold-up style is not flagged as redistributed, carry the clearest tactical profile for a race likely to become a cavalry charge inside the final two furlongs. Madjid, John Harrison, Pipily and Moon Warp are all genuine deep hold-up horses shunted into the midfield slots on the map simply because there is no pace to sit behind — they are not natural front-liners and cannot all get their ideal position; whichever of them does get a prominent pitch by default will be racing out of role, which materially undermines their winning prospects. The shape overwhelmingly favours horses with a quick finishing kick who can land a blow from a handy berth in a falsely-run contest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow tempo, sprint finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field crawls through the early stages and the race erupts into a mass sprint inside the final 2f, turning the contest into a flat-out dash for home.
scenarios.body: With no pace-setter to impose structure, the gallop will be pedestrian and runners will bunch into the straight, making position off the final turn the key factor; horses who can quicken sharply from a handy spot rather than needing a true test of stamina will dominate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One horse dictates solo
scenarios.trigger: If one runner — most likely Madjid or John Harrison by default rather than design — finds itself shuffled to the front and sets a modest, controlled tempo.
scenarios.body: Racing out of role but with a clear lead, that horse could steal an uncontested advantage and prove hard to reel in against hold-up rivals who need more gallop to showcase their finishing kick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late closers pounce
scenarios.trigger: If a genuinely testing pace somehow materialises and the race becomes a true stamina examination over the 1m2f trip.
scenarios.body: Horses with proven form over a mile-plus on good ground would benefit from an honest gallop that rewards those who travel well through the race; Ziggy's Avenger's win over 8f on good and Flag Of Eva's placed effort over 10f give them credentials here too.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos splits the field
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of a pace-setter produces erratic positioning, causing runners to fan wide or get trapped on the rail in a messy finish.
scenarios.body: Moon Warp, fresh from a 318-day absence and likely to be ridden conservatively by Luke Morris, and Pipily, stepping up in trip from sprint distances, are vulnerable in any shape, but a chaotic finish occasionally produces a low-weighted surprise from a horse that gets first run.

watchPoints.text: Ziggy's Avenger — watch where Hector Crouch positions him in the early stages; if he secures a handy berth rather than dropping out to the rear in a slow-run race, he becomes the most dangerous runner in a sprint finish.

Moon Warp — the 318-day layoff for Sir Mark Prescott is notable because the trainer rarely runs unprepared horses, but the established pattern of fading late means punters should watch whether he shows any early signs of freshness that might mask a fitness question.

Madjid — Cieren Fallon's instinct will be to settle the horse out the back, but in a field of hold-up types someone has to go forward; watch in the parade ring and early stalls whether Fallon alters his approach, as that would significantly change the race shape.

Pipily — the switch from sprint trips to 1m2f and the addition of headgear are both notable changes; watch whether she travels with any fluency in the first half of the race, as a horse that struggles to settle on debut at the trip will be spent long before the finish.

Flag Of Eva — coming back from 28 days off with only three runs on her record, watch whether she shows any greenness or is settled confidently by Greatrex in the early stages, as her composure through a slow-tempo race will be key to whether she can produce a finish.

races.name: Lodge At The National Stud Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Elan d'Or
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter who can dictate alone at 1m on Good to Firm; Stuart Williams yard is in fair nick (3/21 last 14 days) and Marco Ghiani is a smart front-rider, but the STYLE_FIT flag suggests she is slightly out of her optimal role here — discount sharpness if she has to work harder than expected.|
runners_data.comment: Elan d'Or strung together back-to-back wins three and four starts back, but that promising sequence faded to fifth and then unplaced in his last two starts. He has run over today's trip and going before and holds an official mark of 87, with a rating of 84 here reflecting the recent form dip.

runners_data.name: Lady Mariko
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's four-year-old has a win and a place in her last five on good ground and steps back to a comfortable 1m trip; Cieren Fallon provides a top-level booking boost, though six wins from fifteen similar-going runs and a moderate recent form string (-16060) tempers enthusiasm.|
runners_data.comment: Lady Mariko won five starts back but has since been well held, twice unplaced and twice sixth in the four starts since, including last time out. She has run over today's trip and going before, but bottom of the weights here on a rating of 80, she needs a big reversal of recent form.

runners_data.name: Silca Bay
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's filly arrives on a 15-day turnaround with her best form on good ground over this exact trip (a win at 8f/SOF recently); however, her natural front-running inclination will be frustrated by Elan d'Or's presence, and she carries the redistribution caveat — she is a prominent racer by instinct but cannot expect to hold that berth here.|
runners_data.comment: Silca Bay has been fairly consistent, with three fourths and a win in his last five starts, though a below-par run four starts back is the outlier. He has run over today's trip and going before and his trainer is among the in-form yards at 26 percent in the last fortnight, some encouragement on a modest rating of 81.

runners_data.name: Dovey Moon
runners_data.note: The most interesting profile in the field: four wins from fifteen similar-going runs and a hat-trick of 8f victories including two on Good; J F Egan takes over and Dovey Moon is a genuine front-runner by nature, yet must sit wider and further back than ideal because Elan d'Or occupies the lead — if he can travel smoothly despite the unnatural position, his sharp turn of foot at this trip is the biggest threat.|
runners_data.comment: Dovey Moon has won twice in his last five starts, either side of a seventh, but the sequence has since cooled - unplaced next time, before finishing third last time out. He has run over today's trip and going before, and although only sixth-best of these on a rating of 81, has shown he has more to offer on his day.

runners_data.name: Astrazar
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old won twice earlier in the season and has since hit a flat patch (form: 11-974); a prominent runner with a solid 9/10 record in similar going conditions, and at OR 82 is the best-handicapped horse in the field if reproducing early-season form, but the recent run of disappointing efforts is a concern.|
runners_data.comment: Astrazar opened this sequence with back-to-back wins five and four starts back, and although the form dipped through a ninth and a seventh, he rallied to fourth last time out. He has run over today's trip and going before and is rated 87, second-best in this field, making him a leading threat to our selection.

runners_data.name: Rogue Encore
runners_data.note: A 106-day absence is the major flag; Peter Chapple-Hyam sends him out lightly prepared (0/1 in last 14 days) and his Tapeta-based form string at Southwell (1-5090 mostly on AW) translates poorly to Good to Firm Newmarket turf, with only 3/15 runners finishing in the frame in similar going conditions.|
runners_data.comment: Rogue Encore won five starts back and rates a workable 87, third-best in this field, having also run over today's trip and going before. But he has been well held since - unplaced in two of his last three starts either side of a ninth - and a 106-day absence adds a real fitness question.

runners_data.name: Mythical Guest
runners_data.note: George Margarson's six-year-old has a tidy record of four places in eleven runs on good ground over 1m; last ran just 8 days ago and Luke Morris has to work with a horse that needs room to come late — the honest pace Elan d'Or should set is unlikely to be fast enough to fully suit a genuine hold-up profile, but his consistency at this trip keeps him relevant.|
runners_data.comment: Mythical Guest returned to form with a third last time out just eight days ago, and he has run over today's trip and going before. Though yet to score in this sequence, the level of his placed efforts leaves him the highest-rated of these seven at 88 and the one to beat on figures.

races.paceDynamic: Elan d'Or is the sole confirmed front-runner in a seven-runner field and, with no genuine rival willing or able to press for the lead, should establish an uncontested, metronomic gallop down the Rowley-style July Course straight mile on Good to Firm ground. Behind the leader, Silca Bay and Dovey Moon are both natural prominent types who have been redistributed to a mapped midfield position because the race cannot accommodate three horses on the front end simultaneously — Elan d'Or is most likely to secure the rail and dictate, while Silca Bay and Dovey Moon will have to settle for a position that is not their first preference. Lady Mariko and Astrazar will fill the chasing pack, with Rogue Encore and Mythical Guest operating from the rear as genuine hold-up horses. This shape — a controlled, honest pace set by one uncontested leader — classically favours prominent racers who can travel just off the fretter and pick up in the final two furlongs, meaning the horses best positioned to exploit are those with the tactical speed to track Elan d'Or at close range and quicken past in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Elan d'Or Controls, Chasers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Elan d'Or dictates an unchallenged, even tempo and the field is forced to come from just off the pace.
scenarios.body: Elan d'Or sets a sustainable lead that stretches the field and leaves the two or three lengths she may concede as the limit of her advantage; the horses best placed to reel her in are those sitting second or third early and with the tactical speed to quicken past in the final furlong on quick ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Elan d'Or Holds On Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Elan d'Or's uncontested, relaxed lead proves so economical that she conserves enough energy to repel all challengers in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Racing on a true flat track at Newmarket with no pressure, she travels within herself and her finishing effort is sufficient to deny those making ground from midfield; her form figures of two wins from similar trips at this going band make this a live possibility.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves faster than anticipated and Elan d'Or's lead evaporates, leaving a late-charging opportunity for the backmarkers.
scenarios.body: Rogue Encore and Mythical Guest would need a true test of stamina and a strong pace to mow down the field, conditions that are only marginally possible given the sole front-runner is unchallenged; Mythical Guest has placed four times at this trip and trip in similar going, giving him the best hold-up profile if closers do get a run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Clash, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Silca Bay or Dovey Moon refuses to settle in their unnatural midfield position and surges to challenge Elan d'Or, injecting unexpected pace.
scenarios.body: A contested, pressured pace would unsettle Elan d'Or's rhythm and potentially produce an even-time finish that scrambles the race shape entirely; neither Silca Bay nor Dovey Moon is ideally placed tactically given their redistribution, but this scenario rewards a horse that can handle a muddling, stop-start tempo.

watchPoints.text: Watch Dovey Moon's early position — if J F Egan sends him forward to contest the lead with Elan d'Or the whole race shape changes, injecting a contested pace that could collapse both front-runners and open the race for closers.

Rogue Encore's 106-day absence combined with a trainer strike rate of 0/1 in the last 14 days makes his fitness a significant unknown; if he blows up fitness-wise he will trail in and distort any late-race market reads.

Silca Bay's redistribution from prominent to a forced midfield berth means Oliver Carmichael (7lb claimer) will need to manage a horse operating out of its comfort zone — watch for early restlessness or an over-eager exit from the stalls.

Mythical Guest ran just 8 days ago and while his form is consistent, back-to-back quick turnarounds on fast ground can blunt a hold-up horse's finishing kick — monitor his market move to gauge stable confidence in his recovery.

The going report confirms the 5:25 race is running on Good to Firm despite a nominal Good description — faster ground than expected will favour those with tactical speed near the pace rather than closers having to make up ground from far back.
